methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, constraints, and state transitions. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements. For the original research topic, this meant extracting rules for state transitions (walking, falling, digging, splattering) based on input signals (bump_left, bump_right, ground, dig). For the generated specification, this involved identifying the described combinational and sequential logic, state transition priorities, and output assignments. The goal was to create sets of atomic units that could be compared for Jaccard similarity and coverage analysis.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Lemmings are modeled using a finite state machine.
Lemmings can be in walk_left state.
Lemmings can be in walk_right state.
Lemmings can be in falling state.
Lemmings can be in digging state.
Lemmings can be in splattered state.
walk_left and walk_right outputs indicate direction when on ground and not digging.
Only one of walk_left or walk_right can be 1 at a time.
areset resets Lemming to walk_left state.
If bump_left is 1, Lemming switches to walk_right.
If bump_right is 1, Lemming switches to walk_left.
If both bump_left and bump_right are 1, Lemming switches direction.
Bump inputs are ignored while falling or digging.
When ground becomes 0, Lemming enters falling state and aaah output becomes 1.
If ground remains 0, Lemming continues to fall.
Bump inputs are ignored while falling.
When ground becomes 1 again, Lemming stops falling and aaah becomes 0.
Lemming resumes walking in same direction as before falling.
bump_left or bump_right in same cycle as ground becomes 0 does not change walking direction.
If ground reappears while still falling, bump inputs are ignored.
Lemming can start digging if on ground and dig input is 1.
Lemming continues digging until ground becomes 0.
digging output is 1 while digging.
digging output becomes 0 when ground becomes 0.
Lemming starts falling when ground becomes 0 after digging.
Bump inputs are ignored while digging.
If dig input is 1 when not walking on ground or falling, dig input is ignored.
If Lemming falls for more than 20 clock cycles and then ground becomes 1, Lemming will splatter.
20 clock cycles are counted while ground is 0.
In splatter state, all outputs become 0 and remain 0 until areset.
clk is clock input.
areset is asynchronous reset to walking left.
bump_left indicates bump on the left.
bump_right indicates bump on the right.
ground indicates presence of ground.
dig is input to initiate digging.
walk_left indicates Lemming is walking left.
walk_right indicates Lemming is walking right.
aaah indicates Lemming is falling.
digging indicates Lemming is digging.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk, areset, bump_left, bump_right, ground, dig.
Module top_module has outputs walk_left, walk_right, aaah, digging.
areset is asynchronous reset.
bump_left and bump_right indicate collisions with obstacles.
ground indicates whether the Lemming is on the ground.
dig is a command to start digging.
walk_left and walk_right indicate the Lemming's walking direction.
aaah indicates it is falling.
digging indicates it is digging.
Combinational logic determines outputs based on current state.
Outputs are solely a function of the current state (Moore machine).
Combinational logic determines next_state based on current state and inputs.
Priority of actions is fall > dig > direction change.
SPLAT state forces all outputs to 0.
walk_left = (current_state == WALK_LEFT)
walk_right = (current_state == WALK_RIGHT)
aaah = (current_state == FALLING)
digging = (current_state == DIGGING)
In SPLAT state, all outputs are forced to 0.
next_state logic implements state transition diagram.
WALK_LEFT: If ground == 0, then next_state = FALLING.
WALK_LEFT: Else if dig == 1, then next_state = DIGGING.
WALK_LEFT: Else if bump_left == 1 || bump_right == 1, then next_state = WALK_RIGHT.
WALK_LEFT: Else next_state = WALK_LEFT.
WALK_RIGHT: If ground == 0, then next_state = FALLING.
WALK_RIGHT: Else if dig == 1, then next_state = DIGGING.
WALK_RIGHT: Else if bump_right == 1 || bump_left == 1, then next_state = WALK_LEFT.
WALK_RIGHT: Else next_state = WALK_RIGHT.
FALLING: If ground == 1 and fall_counter >= 20, then next_state = SPLAT.
FALLING: Else if ground == 1 and fall_counter < 20, then next_state = (previous_direction == LEFT) ? WALK_LEFT : WALK_RIGHT.
FALLING: Else next_state = FALLING.
DIGGING: If ground == 0, then next_state = FALLING.
DIGGING: Else next_state = DIGGING.
SPLAT: next_state = SPLAT.
State transitions and output changes occur on the positive edge of the clk signal.
areset signal asynchronously resets the state machine.
Lemming splatters if it falls for more than 20 clock cycles.
Design uses registers to store current state (current_state) and falling counter (fall_counter).
current_state register is updated on the positive edge of the clock or when the areset signal is asserted.
fall_counter register increments when the Lemming is falling (ground == 0) and resets when the Lemming is on the ground (ground == 1).
Next state logic is implemented using combinational logic.
Non-blocking assignments (<=) are used to update the registers in the sequential always block.
